newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds firm, domestic credit numbers awaited.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds firm, domestic credit numbers awaited.

text.p: Irish bonds firmed in thin late trade on Wednesday in line with most of Europe as the market awaited the release of Thursday's domestic end-December credit numbers, dealers said.
"The Irish credit numbers are a biggie. We might see a bit of jitters ahead of that," one dealer said.
Economists' forecasts range from 15 to 17 percent for credit growth in the month of December from 16.4 percent at end-November.
"It has been quite a strong day. We've seen a recovery by peripherals in Europe, a reversal of recent trends, which has benefited Ireland," one dealer said.

By 1635 GMT, the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 had firmed 55 pence from Tuesday's close at 110.00 to yield 6.55 percent while the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had gained 31 pence from the close at 102.55 to yield 5.85 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds were trading at 90 basis points over German bunds in the 10-year area and 156 basis points over bunds in the five-year area.

Dealers said currency issues look set to top the bill when the world's financial leaders meet in Berlin this week, as a surge in the dollar shared the limelight with the thorny issues of who should join Europe's monetary union and when.
